hypotheses.reasoning: Origin: session-cache restarted at 22:04:17 after node replacement with no RDB snapshot, so it started with 0 keys (#2828). Its traffic was not warm-started, so account-svc session-cache miss ratio jumped to 93% (baseline 6%) and then 99%, with every login falling through to accounts-db (#2887, #2982). accounts-db, which had been healthy with 0 errors, then saturated: a seq scan on audit_log (#2897), connections 490/500 with CPU at 98% (#2921), then slow account lookups and account-svc query timeouts (#3045). Edge-proxy 504s on POST /login (#3049) are the symptom at the edge. The trigger (one cache restart) is small; the damage comes from the miss stampede onto the database. Ruled out: template-svc/mailer 502/503s and the notify 503s (separate, downstream of notifications, not on the login path); status-poller's legacy-inventory timeouts (unrelated deprecated endpoint); metrics-agent drops (telemetry only); billing-reconciler and audit-consumer (healthy). auth-svc had no errors. The audit_log seq scan may be a secondary load contributor but does not explain the timing.

Alternative reading: accounts-db itself ran out of connections and CPU (490/500 slots, CPU 98-100%) and the seq scan on audit_log drove the load. But the saturation began right after the session-cache restart and the miss ratio spike, so the database was overloaded by the cache miss traffic rather than being the origin.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restore session-cache warmth (fix the snapshot/persistence gap that caused the empty restart), add shedding or rate limiting for cache-miss lookups against accounts-db, add an index on audit_log(created_at) to remove the seq scan, and monitor the session-cache miss ratio and restart events.
